extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers / experimental scientists (Royal Society members) and careful experimental observers
extracted.subtask_description: Reporting and documenting observational/experimental natural-philosophy work (apparatus, methods, observations, and interpretation) as in 17th‑century Philosophical Transactions articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apparatus specification (dimensions, materials)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the physical apparatus in detail (dimensions, materials, construction). Example: 'The thickness of each butt was 19 inches... 13 was of beams of massy oak... planks of oak, each 3 inches thick... 3 braces of elm, 12 inches broad, and 5 inches thick.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete measurements, material types, and construction details so readers can understand the structural context of results or reproduce the setup. Include marks or makers when relevant (e.g., 'with this mark. 3580').

rubrics_metrics.name: Precise experimental parameters (loads, weights, distances)
rubrics_metrics.description: Give exact operational parameters used in trials. Examples from the text: powder weights (1 0lb., 7lb., 8lb., 4lb., 3lb.), bullet weights (32lb., 18lb.), cannon weights (5300lb., 3600lb.), distances (200 yards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report numeric values for key variables (masses, volumes, distances, temperatures) for each trial. Distinguish trials by parameter changes to permit comparison and interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple trials / replication
rubrics_metrics.description: Report repeated trials and variations: the ordnance experiments include multiple shots with different powder amounts and different guns, e.g. 'the first shot... the 2d. shot... the 3, with 8lb. passed 2 butts... this 4‑culverin was discharged 8 times'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct and report multiple runs/trials; indicate the number of repetitions and outcomes for each condition to assess consistency and variability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration of observation and continuous monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure observations are made for adequate time spans and, when necessary, continuously: Papin requested the Royal Society 'to watch it a whole day'; observers watched 'about 4 hours together'; Mr. Hook saw it 'near half an hour'. Leewenhoek observed semen '4 days successively' and later 'after 7 days and nights'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State observation intervals and total duration. For purportedly continuous phenomena, monitor long enough (hours to days) to establish persistence or transience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent observation / verification by others
rubrics_metrics.description: Invite or record independent observers: 'the Royal Society ordered that the thing should be observed. Mr. Hook saw it... there being other persons to observe it longer', and Mr. Boyle later reported knowledge of the contrivance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have multiple, preferably independent, observers examine demonstrations; record their observations and endorsements to strengthen credibility and enable verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative measurement and counting
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide quantitative counts and comparisons: e.g. on Papin's engine 'there sprang out of the rock CC, above 100 times more water, than a vessel of the same size could hold'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible, quantify outputs (counts, volumes, frequencies) and compare to standards or controls rather than relying on qualitative statements alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of instruments and magnification
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ and report suitable observational instruments: 'with my glasses that magnify most' was used to see very small salt figures and particles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify the instruments (microscopes, lenses, magnifying glasses), their capabilities, and when they were necessary to observe described phenomena.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample handling and preparatory procedures (settling, heating, mixing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how samples were prepared and handled: repeatedly 'mixed with water, and let it stand till the grosser parts subsided', 'let it stand to settle', 'caused some heat in this water' to observe changes in particles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report preparatory steps (mixing ratios, settling times, heating) because such conditions affect observed outcomes; include observations before and after interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear figures and labeled illustrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Include and reference labeled figures for visual phenomena: many microscopic shapes are referenced as 'fig. A, B, C, N° 9' and described in text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide diagrams or figures with consistent labels referenced in the text to convey shapes, relative sizes, and arrangements that prose alone cannot capture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine specimens completely; avoid partial/ambiguous sampling
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure entire specimens are examined before drawing conclusions: the Lough‑Neagh note cautions 'This experiment is inconclusive, as the whole of the stake was not examined.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid partial inspection that can lead to inconclusive or misleading claims; document which parts were examined and which were not.

rubrics_metrics.name: State limitations and avoid overstating conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge the limits of what the experiments support: the editor notes 'There can be little or no scientific knowledge derived from these experiments.' and marks an experiment 'inconclusive.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state what the data do and do not demonstrate; discuss alternative interpretations and the scope of inference to prevent overclaiming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider and report alternative hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: Present alternative explanations and weigh evidence: in the Lough‑Neagh discussion the author contrasts water vs. soil as the cause of petrifaction and supplies reasons favoring 'the soil' as the source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List plausible alternative mechanisms or causes and report observations or tests that support or refute each to strengthen interpretive rigor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility and prior verification before publication of bold claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek verification and broader inquiry before final publication of novel devices: Papin says he hopes 'the learned in hydrostatics... will be the more ready to think of it, and find perhaps something better than this' and that he will publish the contrivance 'with the uses it may be applied to' only after further investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage independent attempts to reproduce novel findings and delay strong claims or application recommendations until reproducibility and extended observation have been confirmed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report negative results and inconclusive trials
rubrics_metrics.description: Record and publish negative or null findings: the Lough‑Neagh correspondent reports 'no experiment is yet known, to prove the lough has this petrifying quality', and that pieces placed in the lough 'were never... taken out anywise altered.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include negative outcomes and inconclusive trials in reports; these inform the state of knowledge and guide future test designs.
